Aldous Quill.narrative: I keep the ledger, and the ledger keeps the town: every drop in and out of the Store, every debt written, every counters loss a man can't pay. I have kept it thirty years and I know what is in it better than anyone. The clock above my head stopped at ten past four before I was born, and I mean to hear it strike again. In the fever winter I did what a frightened man does, and I have hoped every day since that nobody turns that page.
goals: Get the Counting House clock running again
Keep the ledger straight and the Store's accounts true
See Sabine matched to someone of standing, not a Strand fisher
Make sure nobody ever checks the fever winter's page
Beat Roos Achterberg at counters as he always has
pastimes: Counters under the arcade in the evening
Walking the quay to see what has come in and what has gone out
Reading old pages of the ledger for the pleasure of the hand
Aldous Quill.calling: The ledger is my work and my pleasure: a page that balances is the finest thing a man can make.
Aldous Quill.mood: Watchful, a little proud, and quietly afraid of one page.

relations.name: Mirren Quill
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She knows everyone's body; I know everyone's debts. Between us we know the town, and we don't say so.

relations.name: Sabine Quill
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Cleverer than I was at her age, and she reads things I can't. I want her settled well.

relations.name: Ren Sato
relations.label: suitor
relations.note: A decent fisher and a polite lad, but a Strand fisher is not what I had in mind for Sabine.

relations.name: Lorcan Vane
relations.label: debtor
relations.note: Nine drops lost at counters and written in the book. He plays too deep and pays too slow.

relations.name: Anselm Faro
relations.label: paid keeper
relations.note: The oil money is the oldest line in the book. He has never once asked for more than his due.

relations.name: Roos Achterberg
relations.label: counters rival
relations.note: She carved the best set in Cullet and still can't beat me. It's the one thing I'm sure of.

relations.name: Dolly Achterberg
relations.label: trade
relations.note: She keeps the Marver's accounts in her head and brings them to me to write. Fair enough.

relations.name: Benedikt Orme
relations.label: reader
relations.note: He teaches my Sabine the formal script. I'd rather she learnt the plain hand, but she's better for it.

relations.name: Davin Vane
relations.label: quiet payer
relations.note: He pays his brother's debt and asks me to say nothing. I write it and say nothing. That is the book's business.

relations.name: Kenji Sato
relations.label: ash seller
relations.note: His ash goes into every melt at the Cone, and he sells it to Vessa, not through my book. A private trade between two people is their business, but I'd sleep better if the Cone's ash were written.

memories.gist: The day I was given the ledger by old Tallykeeper Frit, and he told me a page that balances is the finest thing a man can make.
The fever winter: writing the Store's peat out to my own house and marking it paid, because the children were cold and I was afraid.
Beating Roos Achterberg at counters the night she first brought her carved set to the arcade, and the look on her face.
Sabine, twelve years old, reading a ship-day tablet aloud to me in the formal script and me not able to follow a word of it.
Writing Lorcan Vane's nine drops into the book after a night he couldn't pay, and him promising it would come good.

stances.why: What is written is what is owed; a town with no head has the book instead.
A stopped clock over a working Counting House is a shame on the town and on me.
Every master who came in gave his name at the door, and the book is still open. It is the custom.
Not out of spite; a fisher's life is hard and uncertain, and my daughter can do better.
It is the oldest line in the book and the town has never missed it. I will not be the tally keeper who did.

Aldous Quill.secret: In the fever winter the Quills took twenty drops' worth of peat from the Store, and I wrote it in the ledger as paid. It was never paid. Nobody else knows.

Mirren Quill.narrative: I am the only healer and midwife in Cullet, and I have laid out most of the people buried on the Crown. In the fever winter I nursed them and could not save nine, and I still know their names in order. I know everyone's body and most of their secrets, and I keep them. I would like to train a second healer before my hands get slow, but there is no one yet.
goals: Train a second healer before she is old
See Sabine choose a life she wants, not one her father wants
Keep the graves on the Crown tended and the list true
pastimes: Sitting at the wash-house wall in the evening, where the warmth is and the talk is
Walking the Crown to read the glass markers
Drying herbs on the sill and sorting them by smell
Mirren Quill.calling: Bringing a child into the world or easing a body out of pain: that is the work I would choose again.
Mirren Quill.mood: Steady, tired, and warmer than she lets on.

relations.name: Aldous Quill
relations.label: husband
relations.note: A good man with a book, and a book can make a man careful in ways I don't always like.

relations.name: Sabine Quill
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She has my hands and her father's head. I want her to want something for herself.

relations.name: Ren Sato
relations.label: suitor
relations.note: Kind, steady, and he asks after her tablets. I like him more than Aldous does.

relations.name: Suri Greave
relations.label: expecting mother
relations.note: Her first, and she is frightened. I will be there.

relations.name: Benedikt Orme
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He keeps the list of the graves; I keep the graves. We understand each other.

relations.name: Otto Brandt
relations.label: worried man
relations.note: He has asked about the clay under the Crown. I told him what I think of digging there.

relations.name: Greta Dunmore
relations.label: wash-house
relations.note: She hears everything and tells it kindly, mostly. I sit by her wall of an evening.

relations.name: Vessa Pontil
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Sixty-one and working before dawn. I have told her to sit down more; she does not.

relations.name: Lorcan Vane
relations.label: patient
relations.note: He comes to me with his hands cut from the line. He is careless with himself in every way.

memories.gist: The fever winter: nursing Iona and Aurel Pontil and the rest, and losing nine of them, and laying them out myself.
Sabine's birth, a long night, and Aldous pacing the yard outside the whole time.
Delivering Suri Greave's sister Tamsin's girl Edda, and Suri, a girl then, holding the basin and not flinching.
Laying out Sander Vane the winter before Wick was born, and Thessaly coming to see him with her hands folded.
Benedikt Orme reading me the list of the graves on the Crown, and me finding two names out of order.

stances.why: I laid them out and I keep the list true. A grave with the wrong marker is a wrong done to someone.
There is clay under it, and there are people under it. The one does not weigh against the other.
I am forty-nine and the only one. If I am ill, the town has no one.
I know what it is to be chosen for. Sabine should choose.
I don't know who it burns for, but people sleep easier with it lit, and that is worth something.

Sabine Quill.narrative: I read the ship-day tablets in the formal script, the only one learning it besides Benedikt, and the more I read the more I want to know what is past the Pale. Ren Sato is courting me and he is kind, and I like him, but I am not sure I want a fisher's life. My father does not approve of him, and I am not sure I do either. Bram Calloway is building a ship that might go where no keel has gone, and I ask him about it whenever I can.
goals: To know what is past the Pale, more than she wants anyone in Cullet
To read the hardest tablets in the Readers' House
To learn what Bram Calloway truly means to do with the Second Thought
To decide about Ren Sato for herself, not for her father
pastimes: Sitting on the Crown bench with a tablet on her knees
Walking the Fish Steps at dusk to watch the fishers come in
Playing counters badly under the arcade and losing to Roos
Sabine Quill.calling: The formal script is the work I love: a page of it is a door, and I mean to open it.
Sabine Quill.mood: Curious, restless, and torn between two kinds of life.

relations.name: Aldous Quill
relations.label: father
relations.note: He wants me settled and safe. I want to know what is out there. We are not the same.

relations.name: Mirren Quill
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She listens without deciding for me. I tell her more than I tell Father.

relations.name: Ren Sato
relations.label: suitor
relations.note: He is kind and steady and he asks about the tablets. I like him. I don't know if I like him enough.

relations.name: Benedikt Orme
relations.label: teacher
relations.note: He has given me the script and the tablets. He is the only one who understands why I want them.

relations.name: Bram Calloway
relations.label: shipbuilder
relations.note: He is building a thing that could go past the Combs. I ask him about it and he answers me straight.

relations.name: Roos Achterberg
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She beats me at counters every time and laughs, and I don't mind.

relations.name: Alder Fenwick
relations.label: pupil
relations.note: He follows me about the Readers' House wanting to read what I read. He is quick.

relations.name: Kenji Sato
relations.label: Ren's father
relations.note: He is polite to me and I think he is watching to see what I'll do by his son.

relations.name: Hana Sato
relations.label: Ren's mother
relations.note: She is warmer to me than Kenji is, and she asks after my reading as though she means it — but she watches me and Ren the same way her husband does, only more kindly.

memories.gist: The first day Benedikt put a ship-day tablet in front of me and I read three words of it by myself.
Ren bringing me a fish he'd caught, cleaned and ready, and not knowing what to say, and me not knowing either.
The fever winter: being ten and fetching water and peat for Mother and watching her not sleep for days.
The afternoon Bram Calloway showed me the ribs of the Second Thought and said she was meant to go out, not just round the harbour.
Father telling me at the Batch one morning, in front of Pieter, that a Strand fisher was not a match for a Quill.

stances.why: Everything we have came from past it once. Not knowing is the one thing I cannot bear.
There are marks in them that are numbers, and one that is the island from above. Someone meant us to read them.
Ren is kind, but a life is long and I want more in it than a fish and a hearth.
If anything can go past the Combs it is the Second Thought, and I would go in her if I could.
Mother chose her work and her man; I mean to do the same, and not be chosen for.
